concepts.title: Endocrine Glands and Hypothalamus-Pituitary Axis
concepts.definition: The human endocrine system includes the hypothalamus controlling the pituitary through releasing and inhibiting hormones, and the pituitary with its anterior lobe secreting growth hormone, prolactin, thyroid stimulating hormone, adrenocorticotropic hormone, luteinising hormone and follicle stimulating hormone, and posterior lobe storing oxytocin and vasopressin.
concepts.key_idea: The hypothalamus acts as the master control linking neural and endocrine systems, while the anterior pituitary hormones regulate other endocrine glands, making it the master gland.

concepts.title: Thyroid, Parathyroid, Thymus, Adrenal and Pineal Hormones
concepts.definition: The thyroid secretes tetraiodothyronine and triiodothyronine with iodine for basal metabolic rate and the calcium lowering hormone calcitonin, the parathyroid secretes parathyroid hormone raising blood calcium, the thymus secretes thymosins for immunity, the adrenal cortex releases glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids with the medulla releasing adrenaline and noradrenaline, and the pineal secretes melatonin for the sleep wake cycle.
concepts.key_idea: Calcitonin and parathyroid hormone act antagonistically on blood calcium, and adrenal medullary hormones prepare the body for emergency reactions.

concepts.title: Pancreatic and Gonadal Hormones
concepts.definition: The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete glucagon from alpha cells raising blood glucose by glycogenolysis and insulin from beta cells lowering blood glucose by cellular uptake, while the testes secrete androgens like testosterone and the ovaries secrete estrogens and progesterone for reproduction and secondary sexual characters.
concepts.key_idea: Insulin and glucagon act antagonistically to maintain glucose homeostasis, and disorders of this balance produce diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia and loss of glucose through urine.

solution_steps.explain: Note the secreting cell type and its hormone.

concepts.title: Mechanism of Hormone Action and Hormone Disorders
concepts.definition: Water soluble hormones bind surface receptors and act through second messengers like cyclic AMP, while steroid hormones enter cells and bind intracellular receptors regulating gene expression; hormonal disorders include gigantism and acromegaly from excess growth hormone, dwarfism from its deficiency, diabetes insipidus from vasopressin deficiency, simple goitre from iodine deficiency and Cushing's disease from cortisol excess.
concepts.key_idea: Hormones act in very low concentrations through specific receptors, and hypo or hyper secretion of the same hormone produces opposite disorders such as dwarfism and gigantism.

solution_steps.explain: Note whether the hormone acts through surface or intracellular receptors.
Follow second messenger cascades or gene regulation.
